Me and at least one other person, excluding the person(s) being addressed. (exclusive us.)
We, used in the same circumstances where “me” would be used instead of “I”, e.g. for the pronoun in isolation or as the complement of the copula
ex: Who's going to go? — Us. We'll go.

senses.def: Any entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with, such as place of employment or education, nation, region, language, etc.
ex: It's not true that the rest of Europe hates us.
I went to watch my favourite team play Real Madrid, but they thrashed us 5-0.
Come on! Wakey wakey! Let's get us up and out of bed, please.

senses.def: Used to imply connection between the speaker's experiences or activities and a group of listeners.
ex: Hey guys, in this video I'll show you how I make my upside-down sponge cake. First let's get us a few ingredients that we'll need ...
Give us a look at your paper.
Fetch us a cold beer from the fridge, would you.
Look at us while ye’re speakin tiv us.
Could ye dee that for us?

senses.def: Designates the speaker(s)/writer(s) as constituting or belonging to the stated category of people (objective case).
ex: It's not good enough for us teachers.
We'll have to throw us food out.

senses.def: The relationship between the speaker and some other unspecified person.
ex: Us is the best thing that's ever happened to me.
